title: Ensuring Housing Needs of Singles and Singaporeans are Met
what_it_is: Ensuring Housing Needs of Singles and Singaporeans are Met

sections.label: Lowering singles' BTO eligibility age
sections.summary: The Workers' Party proposes lowering the BTO eligibility age for singles to 28 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As set out in the Workers’ Party manifesto, and as reiterated by Leader of the Opposition Mr Pritam Singh in the MND Committee of Supply debate earlier this year, we believe this threshold can and should be lowered and we propose to lower the BTO eligibility age for singles to 28 years, which is when most Singaporeans would have been in the workforce for a few years and have begun to lead more independent lives.

sections.label: BTO application rates and resale prices
sections.summary: Application rates for 2-room Flexi and larger flats reached record highs, and HDB resale prices rose 25% in three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Following the February, May and August BTO exercises this year, application rates for 2-room Flexi flats and 3-room and larger flats have increased even further and reached new record highs, at 5.1 times and 7.2 times respectively this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While I acknowledge that our proposal on singles’ BTO eligibility could increase marginal demand for 2-room Flexi flats, it does not detract from the fact that there appears to be serious imbalances in the housing market, the spillover effects of which is evident for all to see in the secondary market, where HDB resale prices have increased by 25% in the last three years, with prices today 12% higher, compared to just one year ago, and prices showing no signs of slowing down, increasing by 2.8% in just the last three months alone.

sections.label: BTO waiting time up to 5.7 years
sections.summary: With waiting times up to 5.7 years, a successful 28-year-old applicant would be close to 35 when the flat is move-in ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, with a waiting time of up to 5.7 years as of the August 2022 BTO launch, assuming one is successful in balloting for a flat on the first attempt at age 28, he or she would already be close to 35 years old by the time the flat is in a move-in condition.

sections.label: Monthly repayment for 2-room Flexi flat
sections.summary: Indicative prices near S$100,000 for a 2-room Flexi flat in non-mature towns mean monthly repayments of about $400 over 25 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on indicative prices of close to S$100,000 for a 2-room Flexi flat in non-mature towns in the latest August BTO launch, the monthly repayment amount over a 25-year period is only around $400 a month, a fraction of what it costs to rent in the open market.

sections.label: Singles proportion among citizens aged 30-34
sections.summary: SingStat data shows singles among citizens aged 30 to 34 reached a record 42.2% in 2021, up from 27.6% in 2000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on data from SingStat, the proportion of singles among citizens in the 30 to 34 years age group is now at a record high of 42.2% in 2021, increasing steadily from 27.6% in 2000 and 36.9% in 2010.

sections.label: Persons under 35 living alone
sections.summary: DOS data shows persons aged below 35 living alone almost doubled from 12,300 in 2017 to 25,000 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: DOS data shows that between 2017 and 2020, the number of persons aged below 35 and living alone has almost doubled from 12,300 to 25,000.

sections.label: BTO application rates
sections.summary: Since 2015, first-timer application rates for 2-room flexi BTO flats stayed below one time, while 3-room or larger flats were consistently oversubscribed multiple times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, in the BTO exercises since 2015, the application rate for 2-room flexi flats among first-timers have consistently been less than one time, while that for 3-room or larger BTO flats has consistently been multiple times oversubscribed.

sections.label: Singles' BTO eligibility and supply
sections.summary: The speaker urges increasing public housing supply and lowering singles' BTO eligibility age from 35 to 28, noting a reallocation of 2-room flexi flats for singles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope we can, firstly, take urgent and decisive steps to increase the availability of public housing and address the current demand-supply imbalance; and, secondly, lower singles’ eligibility age for HDB BTO flats from the current 35 to 28.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am comforted that there is a slight reallocation of 2-room flexi BTO flats in non-mature areas for singles, with up to 65% of the non-senior 2-room flexi flats in non-mature estates will be set aside for first-timer singles, an increase from up to 50% currently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This, however, only means a marginal increase of, at most, 9% of 2-room flexi flats in only non-mature estates available.

sections.label: Home ownership and singles' housing
sections.summary: Citing Sim Ann on home ownership giving stability, security and belonging, the speaker hopes the Government considers the points raised on singles' housing needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann shared last year that beyond just a roof over our heads, home ownership has provided Singaporeans with a sense of stability, security and belonging and has given us a strong stake in our country’s progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In this spirit, I hope the Government can consider the points I have raised in this speech and ensure that the housing needs of singles and all Singaporeans are met.

sections.label: Ramping up BTO supply
sections.summary: The Government is working with the COVID-19-hit construction industry to ramp up BTO supply to 100,000 flats till 2025, if demand and circumstances warrant it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We are also taking steps to raise the housing supply.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We are working hard, working with the construction industry that has been severely impacted because of the COVID-19 pandemic to ramp up BTO supply to 100,000 flats till 2025, if demand and circumstances warrant it.

sections.label: Singles' quotas and housing grants
sections.summary: The non-senior quota rose from 50% to 65% from the August 2022 BTO exercise, and eligible first-timer singles can get grants up to $40,000 for new and $80,000 for resale flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Specifically, we raised the non-senior quota from 50% to 65% with effect from the August 2022 BTO exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: And eligible first-timer singles can also qualify for various housing grants – up to $40,000 for a new flat purchase and $80,000 for a resale flat purchase.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We have taken steps to adjust, to finetune our policies, trying to meet the needs and aspirations of all Singaporeans within the constraints of the land and resources that we have.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: There is also another trend that we have observed where more singles and young couples are renting.

sections.label: Co-living and shared housing
sections.summary: An increasingly popular housing trend, especially among youths, is co-living or shared housing arrangements with common facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: An increasingly popular housing trend, especially amongst the youths, is in the form of co-living or shared housing arrangements with common facilities.

sections.label: Singles housing age eligibility
sections.summary: The government will review housing options with private actors and discuss lowering singles' age eligibility from 35 to 28 under Forward Singapore, noting land constraints and market risks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: It is not just public housing and private housing, but also commercial providers with rental options.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We will continue to review developments holistically and comprehensively and assess if there would be ways to work with the private actors to meet the demand from youths and singles.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State, you have a minute and a half.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And to Mr Louis Chua's point about lowering the age eligibility from 35 today to 28 for the housing market for singles, this is an issue that we have discussed before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We will, certainly, engage these issues as part of our Forward Singapore discussions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: But there are considerations that still remain – there are binding constraints in terms of land resources as well as implications on the housing market with enhanced demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We have to bear in mind that supply is inelastic while demand can change very quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: That might lead to high prices and those at the margins – especially those vulnerable singles like the elderly singles, single parents and those in need of housing urgently – might be squeezed out.
